objective: Define in general terms, in the root's asking rules, what makes a question unnecessary, so the root never asks one, with the merge, method and branch cases only as illustrations.
scope: Worktree /home/user/holyagent-hook-locks, branch release/0.2.0/fix/no-merge-question, with uncommitted changes from the previous writer (merge question removed; a new asking.md bullet saying a choice the repository convention or a holyagent default settles is applied and recorded, never asked; R-DEFAULTS, R-MERGEWAIT, R-S-HEAD). The maintainer's words: 'in general, unnecessary questions must not be asked' and 'but it must define generically what that means'. Write one general test in packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/root/asking.md (and wherever the root rules restate when to ask, such as the task-list/AskUserQuestion rule and user-messages.md, so they agree): a question is unnecessary when its answer would not change what the root does, or when something already settles it (the user's words or an earlier answer, the repository's conventions, a holyagent default or recommended option, the code, or a fact a specialist can establish).
